report:
## Research Findings

The claim that influenza vaccination *causes* Alzheimer's disease is not supported by scientific evidence — in fact, the strongest and most recent research points in the opposite direction.

**Origin of the myth:** The claim traces back largely to remarks by Hugh Fudenberg, whose unpublished, non-peer-reviewed assertions have been widely debunked. Fact-checking organizations have explicitly rated the claim false or unsupported (https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/flu-shot-avoidance/).

**Evidence pointing the other direction:** Multiple large cohort studies and a recent (2026) analysis in *Neurology* of nearly 200,000 adults aged 65+ found that high-dose influenza vaccination was associated with a *reduced* risk of Alzheimer's dementia compared to standard-dose vaccination, with a stronger protective effect in women (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214782). A systematic review of vaccination broadly (including flu, shingles, pneumococcal, Tdap) similarly found associations with *lower* dementia risk (https://academic.oup.com/ageing/article/54/11/afaf331/8339764). An Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation review states plainly: "There is no peer-reviewed scientific evidence supporting this claim... instead there is evidence to support an association between getting the flu shot and a decreased risk for dementia" (https://www.alzdiscovery.org/cognitive-vitality/blog/is-there-a-link-between-alzheimers-disease-and-the-flu-shot).

**Caveats:** These are observational/associational studies (not randomized trials for dementia outcomes), so causality for the protective effect isn't fully proven either, and some critics note effect sizes may be modest in absolute terms. Separate debates exist about vaccine adjuvants (aluminum) and Alzheimer's, but reviews there also find no established causal link.

**Conclusion:** The evidence does not support that flu vaccines cause Alzheimer's; current data suggest a possible protective association instead.
